answer: Each identity registers as one vertex on the lotus ledger with its copper and jobs; a vertex is paid only for covered jobs, at 12 copper per job, so 10 jobs need 120 copper locked to that vertex. One vertex's copper cannot cover another, so the k-th fake needs its own 120 copper; 1,000 fakes claiming 10 jobs each lock 120,000 copper. An auditor recomputes each ratio from the lotus ledger; uncovered jobs are not paid. A copper-sharing ring fails: copper listed under two vertices is struck from both, zeroing coverage and freezing that copper one epoch. An honest agent locks 120 copper once.
